messages.subject: ddm coding scheme
messages.body_plain:
I was wondering how you implemented the DDM in the choiceRT_ddm_single function. Given that the model only requires choices and RTs as input, it's unclear to me how it is able to estimate both drift and starting point. If I treat ‘choices’ as reflecting the actual response, than the model doesn’t know what the "correct" response was (i.e., because it doesn’t know which stimulus was presented) so I don’t get how it can estimate drift rate. If I treat ‘choices’ as reflecting the accuracy (correct or wrong) than I don’t understand how it estimates starting point – as that concept doesn’t make sense in an accuracy coding scheme.

Any input much appreciated!

Best wishes,

messages.body_plain:
Hi Oli,

Thanks for your contribution to hBayesDM!

Those Python codes (convert-to-r.py and convert-to-py.py) use `pathlib.Path` to handle file paths. However, it seems that Python 3.5 has an unexpected incompatibility with it.

Instead, I just checked that it perfectly works with Python 3.6 and above. Could you set up your Python environment with a higher version and try it out?

I will edit the contribution wiki page as it requires Python 3.6 or above, too. Sorry for your inconvenience.

Best,
Jaeyeong
